clue.text: Flat hair — because it's been slept on?

parts.note: mat (also spelt matt) describes a flat, non-glossy finish
a tress is a long lock of hair

explanation.surface: Someone's hair is flattened, presumably because they have been lying on it.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is playful: the thing slept on is the bed's padding, not the hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed's padded base is what a sleeper lies on all night.

clue.text: Copper in a box left out pointedly

indicators.note: in places the copper symbol inside the rest of the build
out tells us the letter for left is dropped from the television word

parts.note: the box is British slang for the television, the telly
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A copper coin sits in a box from which something has been left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' drops L from TELLY, leaving TELY; CU goes 'in' after A to give A-CU-TELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking acutely means sharply and with keen point, the same as speaking pointedly.

clue.text: Venture to say goodbye

explanation.surface: Someone dares to bid farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: To 'take leave to' doubt something is a formal way to dare or presume; to take your leave is to depart with a farewell.

clue.text: College includes American training centre!

indicators.note: includes means the college name holds the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: Eton College, the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A college has an American training centre attached.
explanation.walkthrough: EUSTON is a major London railway terminus; the exclamation mark signals the pun on 'training' as a place full of trains.
explanation.definitionFit: A London mainline railway terminus is a centre for trains, punningly a train-ing centre.

clue.text: Flower is getting smaller — not the sort to come out

definitions.text: not the sort to come out

explanation.surface: A wilting bloom that stays shut, unwilling to open.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase is a bloom that is diminishing; idiomatically it names a very shy person who avoids the limelight.

clue.text: Oppressor of the French soil

parts.note: de is the French word for of
to soil something is to spot or stain it

explanation.surface: A tyrant who oppresses the French land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soil' looks like a noun meaning earth, but it is a verb meaning stain.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant rules oppressively, the classic sense of an absolute ruler.

clue.text: Girl, very French, on board ship in trouble

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

indicators.note: on board puts the French word inside the ship's letters, like cargo aboard

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
tres is the French word for very

explanation.surface: A girl, very French in style, is aboard a ship that is in difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in serious difficulty or danger is being in a state of anguish or peril.

clue.text: Did her box contain Post Office letters to an artist?

parts.note: the letters of the abbreviation PO are P and O, written out as words
RA, Royal Academician, stands for an artist

explanation.surface: A question about a box holding letters posted to a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth she opened a box (a jar) that released all the world's evils; the letters P 'and' O are written out.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the first woman was given a jar or box that held all evils.

clue.text: Dealing with a case, Trent met with a disaster

indicators.note: a disaster wrecks things, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A man called Trent met with calamity while handling a legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: TRENT, MET and the second 'a' are rearranged; 'with' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: How a doctor or lawyer handles a patient or matter is their handling or management of it.

clue.text: In the loose scrums, university causes commotion

indicators.note: In places the university letter within the rugby term

parts.note: in rugby a ruck is a loose scrum formed over the ball on the ground

explanation.surface: During loose rugby scrums, a university side stirs up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: A ruck in rugby is a loose scrum formed over the ball on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumpus or uproar is a noisy disturbance.

clue.text: Congregationalist's reaction to priest

parts.note: in church services the congregation answers the priest's lines with set replies

explanation.definitionFit: In liturgy, the set words spoken by the people in reply to the minister are their answers.

clue.text: Unfurl almost new brolly from good stock

indicators.note: unfurling opens out and rearranges, so these letters are reordered
almost means the last letter is dropped from the umbrella word

explanation.surface: Open up a nearly new umbrella of fine pedigree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' leaves BROLL from BROLLY (British slang for an umbrella); with NEW it is rearranged by 'Unfurl'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being of noble or aristocratic birth means coming from a good family line.

clue.text: Rumour you must have heard

explanation.surface: A piece of gossip that surely reached your ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearsay or common talk is one sense; the loud bang of a gun firing is the other.

clue.text: In Chernobyl, a wise local regulation

indicators.note: In signals the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A sensible rule at the Chernobyl nuclear site.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule made by a town council or local authority is a municipal ordinance.

clue.text: An engagement to marry both later break

indicators.note: break smashes the words apart so their letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Both partners later break off their engagement.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal promise to wed is a betrothal, an old word for an engagement.

clue.text: This sponge has been soaked before it reaches the consumer

definitions.text: This sponge has been soaked before it reaches the consumer

parts.words: This sponge has been soaked before it reaches the consumer
parts.note: a sponge pudding steeped in wine or sherry, so the cake is 'drunk' before anyone eats it

explanation.definitionFit: A traditional British trifle-like dessert is a sponge soaked in alcohol, so it is intoxicated before being eaten.

clue.text: Changed one's position and awoke

explanation.surface: Someone switched sides and regained consciousness.
explanation.definitionFit: To be persuaded to a new view is one sense; to recover consciousness after fainting is the other.

clue.text: Push the grub in to help the silage

parts.note: to lend a hand is to help
silage is fodder, animal feed

explanation.surface: Shove food in to aid the farm's silage.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeding an animal or person manually means putting food into their mouth yourself.

clue.text: Get a guide, perhaps, to the state of the water

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the words could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Fetch a guide to explain how the water stands.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument measuring the sea's level at a harbour reports on its rise and fall.

clue.text: Art style unusual in its propriety

parts.note: Art Deco is a 1920s and 30s design style
rum is British slang for odd or unusual

explanation.surface: An art style that is odd in its correctness.
explanation.definitionFit: Correct and dignified behaviour is good manners or seemliness.

clue.text: Scope for a doctor in the island

indicators.note: in places the doctor's letters inside the island word

parts.note: an ait is a small island in a river
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, stands for a doctor

explanation.surface: Room for a doctor to work on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' looks like a letter in the answer, but it is a link; an AIT (or eyot) is a small island in the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: The extent or range of something is its reach or bounds.

clue.text: The same one of the ears is defective

parts.note: id. abbreviates idem, Latin for the same
I is the Roman numeral one
otic is the medical adjective for of the ear

explanation.surface: One of a matching pair of ears is faulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Being defective in mind, foolish, is to be stupid.

clue.text: Dishonour for Greek character holding the head of Thyestes

indicators.note: holding means the Greek letter keeps another letter inside it

parts.note: sigma is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Disgrace for a Greek hero clutching Thyestes's head, recalling his gruesome myth.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark of disgrace or shame attaching to a person is a stain on their name.

clue.text: Soldiers rebuked for bloomer

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers
chid is an old past tense of chide, to rebuke

explanation.surface: Soldiers were scolded for a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' reads as a blunder; here it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer here is a flowering plant, and this is a showy exotic flower.

clue.text: In summer, for example, team is about to get involved

parts.note: taken as written
summer is an example of a school term

indicators.note: about turns the Roman-numeral team round

parts.note: a cricket or football team is an eleven, XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: During summer a team is about to get involved in something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns XI round to give IX.
explanation.definitionFit: To mix together is to blend or mingle, so to get involved with each other.

clue.text: Prince captures Cade, say, using a plant

indicators.note: captures means the prince's name holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: Prince Hal, the young Henry V in Shakespeare
Jack Cade led a revolt in 1450, so he is an example of an insurgent

explanation.surface: A prince seizes the rebel Jack Cade using some plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Cade led the 1450 Kentish uprising against Henry VI.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluebell-like wild flower is a plant.

clue.text: Fish strung out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A fish hung up on a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A family of tropical sea fish named for the noise they make.

clue.text: Slack journalist proceeded to go slow

parts.note: limp means slack or floppy
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A lazy reporter went at a snail's pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking lamely with an injured leg means moving slowly and unevenly.

clue.text: The Water-carrier used by Niobe

parts.note: Niobe wept endlessly for her children, so her water-carrier is the channel for tears, not Aquarius

explanation.definitionFit: The canal that carries tears from the eye is what a weeping mythological mother would use constantly.
